item.title: Pesquisa do Fed mostra pressões de preços ganhando força em meio a alta de custos dos combustíveis
item.description: O mercado de trabalho dos EUA permaneceu estagnado em um cenário de poucas contratações e demissões em massa, enquanto a inflação se intensificava em várias regiões do país nas últimas semanas, segundo relatório divulgado na quarta-feira pelo Federal Reserve, ressaltando o que está em jogo enquanto o banco central avalia se deve realizar um segundo aumento consecutivo da taxa de juros ainda neste mês.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O mercado de trabalho dos EUA permaneceu estagnado em um cenário de poucas contratações e demissões em massa, enquanto a inflação se intensificava em várias regiões do país nas últimas semanas, segundo relatório divulgado na quarta-feira pelo Federal Reserve, ressaltando o que está em jogo enquanto o banco central avalia se deve realizar um segundo aumento consecutivo da taxa de juros ainda neste mês. Embora as empresas em grande parte do país tenham uma perspectiva positiva, suas “expectativas tendem a ser de um crescimento moderado, com ênfase no setor manufatureiro e prejudicadas por incertezas persistentes”, afirmou o Fed em seu mais recente relatório “Livro Bege”, um compêndio de dados baseados em pesquisas e comentários de empresas compilados por seus 12 bancos regionais para fornecer uma visão das condições econômicas. “As empresas relataram preços elevados do diesel e observaram que as sobretaxas de combustível estavam repassando os custos aumentados por toda a cadeia de suprimentos”, afirmou o relatório. Ele observou que 3 dos 12 distritos do Fed descreveram o aumento dos preços como robusto e 8 como moderado, com 3 deles observando que ele estava “se intensificando”. “Contatos em vários distritos também observaram pressão contínua sobre os preços proveniente de outras commodities, tarifas e seguros”, afirmou o relatório. A pesquisa também funciona como uma espécie de barômetro das pressões econômicas que os eleitores estão enfrentando antes das eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro, que determinarão se o Partido Republicano do presidente Donald Trump manterá o controle do Congresso. O custo de vida é a principal questão citada pelos eleitores em uma pesquisa recente da Reuters/Ipsos. O Fed aumentou sua taxa básica de juros em 0,25 ponto percentual, para a faixa de 3,75% a 4,00%, no mês passado, e a maioria dos formuladores de política monetária indicou que provavelmente será necessário outro aumento este ano, embora provavelmente não antes de dezembro. Os mercados financeiros estão precificando uma probabilidade de cerca de 37% de um aumento dos juros na reunião do Fed de 27 a 28 de outubro, depois que dados divulgados nesta quarta-feira mostraram que os preços ao consumidor (CPI, na sigla em inglês) subiram 3,7% nos 12 meses até setembro, muito mais do que a meta de 2% do banco central e acima da previsão consensual dos economistas consultados pela Reuters. O aumento nos custos da gasolina devido à guerra no Oriente Médio foi o principal responsável pelo aumento do CPI, com os preços em rápida elevação de softwares e brinquedos também apontando para o impacto da demanda impulsionada pela IA e das tarifas mais altas sob a política comercial de Trump. O aumento do custo dos empréstimos para a compra de imóveis é um fardo adicional para muitas famílias americanas. A taxa média das hipotecas de taxa fixa de 30 anos subiu na semana passada para 7,5%, o nível mais alto em quase três anos, informou a Associação dos Bancos Hipotecários na quarta-feira. Os dados para o último “Livro Bege” foram coletados até 5 de outubro. (Reportagem de Ann Saphir)

item.title: Red hot CPI report fuels AI rout
item.description: Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Darshan R, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest [USN:L6N4600XF TEXT:"hot US inflation report"], highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector. Among the [USN:L4N4601KQ TEXT:"leading decliners"] were data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius (NBIS.O) , off 11%, cloud computing giant Oracle (ORCL.N) , down 9%, and AI server seller Dell Technologies (DELL.N) , down 11%. Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value. The declines reflect the impact of tightening financial conditions, as well as the outsize gains scored by some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year — part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector (.SPLRCT) at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations. Concern over rising borrowing costs also weighed on Wednesday's other big decliners. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%. "We're getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave," said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners. Coreweave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said in an internal memo the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. Wednesday's rout is the latest sign of a market struggling to come to grips with the implications of high inflation at a time when AI-fueled corporate borrowing has helped push up global interest rates. Investors generally remain sanguine on the sector in part because its largest players, from chip maker Nvidia (NVDA.O) to the so-called [USN:L4N45T0NO TEXT:"hyperscalers"] — primarily Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Meta (META.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) — are highly profitable and widely perceived as well managed, despite concerns about debt. But higher rates will make borrowing and building costlier, a fact that is likely to hit unprofitable and less-profitable firms first. On Wednesday, US interest rates rose following the hot inflation report, pushing the 30-year yield as high as 5.63% before rates pulled back sharply in the afternoon. "I do think long rates above 5% and creeping towards 6% is a problem for the marginal borrower, I'll call them," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, in an interview with Reuters. "It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers." The Nasdaq (.IXIC) was down 2% on Wednesday afternoon, with Alphabet and the other major hyperscalers mostly down between around 2%. SpaceX (SPCX.O) , another major AI player, was down 3%. "I guess it's grown to a group of five now. SpaceX has kind of joined the party here to join in with like Meta and Microsoft and Google and Amazon," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. "Those five are spending like 75% of the money that's being invested in data centers here in the country. And those five are obviously putting all their profits and then some into these data centers and the returns they're generating from those are really good." Despite the strong economics of these firms and their investments, Ellerbroek said it's not surprising that investors remain skeptical about the AI buildout, in part because of the busts that have preceded this one, particularly the dot-com meltdown that started in 2000. "This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they're investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren't really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late 90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds," Ellerbroek said. "Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They're being very cautious and I think selective."

item.title: Zelenskiy recebe apoio total do Reino Unido depois que Trump se voltou contra ele
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskiy recebeu uma forte demonstração de apoio em Londres nesta quarta-feira, ao se reunir com o primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, e o rei Charles, depois que as relações do líder ucraniano com os Estados Unidos sofreram uma brusca deterioração.
item.dc:creator: William James
item.content:encoded: Volodymyr Zelenskiy recebeu uma forte demonstração de apoio em Londres nesta quarta-feira, ao se reunir com o primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, e o rei Charles, depois que as relações do líder ucraniano com os Estados Unidos sofreram uma brusca deterioração. Zelenskiy foi recebido com todas as honras, chegando ao Reino Unido após mais uma noite de intensos ataques russos e poucas horas depois de a Ucrânia acusar a SpaceX, de Elon Musk, de incapacitar seus drones ao limitar os serviços da Starlink. A demonstração diplomática, que incluiu uma audiência de 25 minutos com Charles e uma guarda de honra em Downing Street, ecoou a visita de Zelenskiy a Londres em fevereiro de 2025, logo após ele ter entrado em conflito com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e seu vice, JD Vance. No início da reunião desta quarta-feira em Downing Street, Zelenskiy disse que queria discutir as dificuldades relacionadas à Starlink e ao compartilhamento de informações de inteligência, e que a Ucrânia ainda contava com sua parceria com os Estados Unidos. Trump afirmou no fim de semana que Zelenskiy deveria ser substituído como líder da Ucrânia, dias depois de ter fechado um acordo com Moscou para suspender as sanções às exportações russas de diesel. O Reino Unido afirmou que não apoia o acordo entre os EUA e a Rússia sobre o diesel e pediu que os aliados mantenham a pressão econômica sobre Moscou. Em entrevista ao jornalista Piers Morgan, Zelenskiy disse que foi doloroso ver Trump tomar o partido da Rússia em detrimento da Ucrânia. Burnham disse que os últimos dias foram “muito sombrios e difíceis” para a Ucrânia, mas que o Reino Unido continuava sendo um aliado firme. “Estamos ao seu lado, e isso não vai mudar”, afirmou. Anteriormente, ele anunciou a entrega planejada de 45 milhões de libras (US$59,60 milhões) em mísseis terra-ar usados para atingir drones russos movidos a jato, com 10 milhões de libras desse pacote sendo liberados em regime de urgência para atender a uma necessidade imediata na Ucrânia. Burnham solicitou que as autoridades elaborassem novas sanções e ajuda militar, e seus ministros das Relações Exteriores e da Fazenda têm pressionado os aliados a seguirem o exemplo do Reino Unido na proibição de serviços marítimos que apoiem as exportações russas de gás natural liquefeito.

item.title: Illinois QB Katin Houser (hand) out 4-6 weeks
item.description: Illinois quarterback Katin Houser underwent a medical procedure on his right (throwing) hand and is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Bret Bielema announced Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Illinois quarterback Katin Houser underwent a medical procedure on his right (throwing) hand and is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Bret Bielema announced Wednesday. Houser sustained the injury while attempting to make a tackle on an interception return in the third quarter of Saturday's 38-37 overtime victory at Michigan State. Michael Clayton II replaced Houser and tossed a 25-yard touchdown pass to Hudson Clement on the first play of overtime in East Lansing, Mich. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns for Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten), which returns to action on Oct. 24 against Oregon in Champaign, Ill. "I had a long conversation with him Sunday night kind of about what it means to be a starting quarterback in this league and in college football," Bielema said of Clayton on Wednesday. "... Excited about his opportunity." Houser, a transfer from East Carolina who began his college career with Michigan State, has completed 66.3% of his passes for 1,440 yards with 12 touchdowns and four interceptions in six games this season. He also has rushed for 120 yards and two TDs. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff qualify for WTA Finals
item.description: Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula both have qualified for the season-ending WTA Finals for a fifth straight year, the WTA announced Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula both have qualified for the season-ending WTA Finals for a fifth straight year, the WTA announced Wednesday. Only eight players qualify to compete in singles at the Nov. 8-15 hard-court tournament in Indian Wells, Calif., which features a $15.5 million prize pool. Gauff defeated China's Qinwen Zheng to win the tournament in 2024, while Pegula lost to Poland's Iga Swiatek in the 2023 final. Gauff, 22, is ranked No. 5 in the world and has won just one title this season at the Cincinnati Open, where she defeated Pegula in straight sets in the final on Aug. 23. Pegula, 32, is ranked No. 4 in the world and has two titles this season at the Dubai Tennis Championships in February and the Charleston Open in March. Also qualified for the WTA Finals are defending champion and World No. 1 Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan, Aryna Sabalenka of Belarus, Mirra Andreeva of Russia and Linda Noskova of the Czech Republic, with two spots still open. --Field level Media

item.title: Racial employment gap widened among new US lawyers, study finds
item.description: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show. More than 94% of 2025’s white law graduates found jobs within 10 months, compared to less than 91% of law graduates of color, according to figures released Wednesday by the National Association for Law Placement. Black law graduates had the lowest employment rate at 87%, down from nearly 90% in 2024, the NALP data showed. The employment rate for 2025 Hispanic law graduates was slightly over 91%, down from more than 92% the previous year. The employment rate for Asian law graduates held steady at about 92%. The relatively small cohort of Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander law graduates posted the highest employment rate at more than 96%. “A law degree should open doors, but NALP's latest report shows that those doors are not equally open to everyone,” NALP Executive Director Nikia Gray said in a statement after releasing the data. The law graduates of 2025 hit the job market amid the Trump administration’s widespread campaign to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion programs in higher education, government and the private sector. In March 2025, the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission [USN:L1N3Q010H TEXT:"demanded detailed hiring data from 20 major firms"], including applicant names and whether race or gender influenced their employment decisions. The US Federal Trade Commission earlier this year [USN:FWN3YV125 TEXT:"warned"] 42 major law firms that their hiring practices may violate federal antitrust law. Diversity Lab, a group that promoted diversity goals at law firms, [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"shuttered"] in June after coming under FTC scrutiny. Many major law firms have publicly withdrawn or altered their public references to diversity, equity and inclusion since Trump returned to the White House, a Reuters special report found . Nearly 50 US law firms that previously provided NALP with demographic data about their lawyers [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"declined to do so"] this year, with NALP attributing the drop to Trump’s crackdown on law firm DEI efforts. Additionally, the US Department of Education is [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"poised to revoke"] the American Bar Association’s status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools, partly because it says the ABA took too long to eliminate DEI standards for schools. According to the new NALP data, white law graduates outpaced every racial group except for Middle Eastern or North African law graduates in securing jobs that require passing the bar — considered the gold standard for legal employment. First-generation college students had a lower employment rate than law graduates whose parents attended college or law school. Read more: [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"Facing DEI pressures, some law firms shield data in latest diversity survey"] [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"Law firm diversity group shutters amid Trump's DEI crackdown"]

item.title: Vinicius recibe suspensión de cuatro partidos y se perderá el Clásico contra el Barcelona
item.description: Vinicius Jr. se perderá el primer Clásico de la temporada del Real Madrid contra el Barcelona, después de que la Comisión Disciplinaria de la Federación Española de Fútbol le impuso el miércoles una sanción de cuatro partidos al delantero brasileño.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vinicius Jr. se perderá el primer Clásico de la temporada del Real Madrid contra el Barcelona, después de que la Comisión Disciplinaria de la Federación Española de Fútbol le impuso el miércoles una sanción de cuatro partidos al delantero brasileño. Vinicius fue expulsado por tirar del pelo a Nathan Saliba tras salir desde el banquillo en la victoria por 1-0 del sábado ante el Villarreal. La comisión le impuso una sanción de dos partidos por la tarjeta roja y le sumó otros dos por sus protestas al árbitro, según el informe disciplinario de la octava jornada de LaLiga. La suspensión deja a Vinicius fuera de los partidos de liga contra el Sevilla, el Barcelona, el Racing de Santander y el Valencia, y a su entrenador, José Mourinho, sin uno de sus delanteros más usados para el desplazamiento al Camp Nou. Vinicius ha sido titular en todos los partidos del Real Madrid esta temporada, salvo uno. Tras el incidente, pidió disculpas a sus compañeros y a la afición del Real Madrid a través de las redes sociales. El Clásico se disputará el 25 de octubre, cuando el Real Madrid viaje para enfrentarse al líder de la liga, el Barcelona. Seis puntos separan a ambos equipos en la clasificación.

item.title: Red Bull boss Laurent Mekies signs multi-year extension
item.description: Max Verstappen has committed to Red Bull's Formula 1 team through 2030, and now the four-time world champion knows he will have continuity, with team principal Laurent Mekies signing a multi-year extension.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Max Verstappen has committed to Red Bull's Formula 1 team through 2030, and now the four-time world champion knows he will have continuity, with team principal Laurent Mekies signing a multi-year extension. The team announced Wednesday that Mekies now is signed through the 2031 season. The 49-year-old Frenchman was promoted in July 2025 following Christian Horner's departure. Mekies had spent six years at Ferrari before joining Red Bull's sister team Racing Bulls in 2023. After watching McLaren claim the 2025 constructors' championship and Red Bull get off to a slow start under the new regulations this season, the team has made steady progress. Verstappen has won consecutive races and sits fourth in the drivers' standings, just eight points behind Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and 17 points behind Mercedes' George Russell. Red Bull's second driver, Isack Hadjar, is eighth in the standings despite missing three races due to injury. Red Bull is also now only seven points behind McLaren for third place in the constructors' standings. "I am incredibly proud to continue this journey with Oracle Red Bull Racing," Mekies said in a statement. "What makes this team special is the way everyone comes together in pursuit of the same goal, and I feel privileged to work alongside such a talented and committed group every day. "As we look ahead, we will continue to embrace the principles that define us: being free in our thinking, fast in our actions and bold in our decisions." Mekies, who has overseen car upgrades throughout this season, thanked Red Bull shareholders Chalerm Yoovidhya and Mark Mateschitz for their continued support. "The strength of Red Bull has always come from its people and from creating an environment where talented individuals can achieve extraordinary things together," Yoovidhya and Mateschitz said in a joint statement. "Laurent has played a crucial role in guiding the team through an important period of transition while maintaining the competitive spirit and the Red Bull principles that define us. "This extension reflects our confidence in his leadership and our shared belief in the long-term vision of the team. We are ambitious about what lies ahead and we are committed to building on this momentum together." --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: FIFA to amend rule that led to Folarin Balogun red-card overturn
item.description: Call it the Folarin Balogun rule.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Call it the Folarin Balogun rule. FIFA is changing its rules to prevent a repeat of the outcry sparked by the reversal of Balogun's red-card ban at this summer's World Cup, ESPN reported Wednesday. The United States forward's red card, and its mandatory one-match suspension, was overturned by FIFA's disciplinary committee and he was allowed to play in a round of 16 match on July 6 against Belgium, which won 4-1. He had received a direct red card in the 64th minute of a July 1 match for a foul on Bosnia and Herzegovina's Tarik Muharemovic. The U.S. went on to win 2-0 with 10 men in the round of 32, and Balogun was suspended for the next game. The controversy deepened when U.S. President Donald Trump admitted he had personally asked FIFA president Gianni Infantino to review the penalty. Infantino has claimed that the disciplinary committee's decision was made without his involvement. When the 37-member FIFA council meets on Thursday, a motion to prohibit future such suspensions of one-match bans will be at the top of the agenda, per ESPN. Even if FIFA amends the rule, the Balogun controversy isn't likely to disappear. FIFA vice president Debbie Hewitt is among the sport's leaders who have asked Infantino to release all documents related to the case. Thursday's FIFA council meeting is the first since Infantino came under fire this summer for a now-tabled plan to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup's commercial business to private investors. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fed survey shows price pressures intensifying amid rise in fuel costs
item.description: The US labor market remained stuck in a low-hire, low-fire state and inflation was intensifying across parts of the country in recent weeks, a Federal Reserve report showed on Wednesday, underscoring what's at stake as the central bank weighs whether to deliver a second straight interest rate hike later this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US labor market remained stuck in a low-hire, low-fire state and inflation was intensifying across parts of the country in recent weeks, a Federal Reserve report showed on Wednesday, underscoring what's at stake as the central bank weighs whether to deliver a second straight interest rate hike later this month. While businesses in much of the country have a positive outlook, their "expectations tend to be for slight growth, weighted toward manufacturing and burdened by persistent uncertainties," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Firms reported elevated diesel prices and noted that fuel surcharges were passing on increased costs throughout the supply chain," said the report. It noted that three of the Fed's 12 districts described price growth as robust and eight as moderate, with three noting it was "intensifying." "Contacts in multiple Districts also noted continued price pressure from other commodities, tariffs, and insurance," it said. The survey also acts as something of a barometer for the economic pressures voters are dealing with ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republican Party maintains control of Congress. The cost of living is the top issue cited by voters in a recent [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll."] The Fed increased its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"3.75%-4.00% range"] last month, and most policymakers have indicated another hike will likely be needed this year, though probably not until December. Financial markets are pricing [USN:L6N4600VL TEXT:"about a 37% chance"] of a rate hike at the Fed's October 27-28 meeting after data on Wednesday showed [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer prices"] rose 3.7% in the 12 months through September, far faster than the central bank's 2% target and above the consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters. Higher gasoline costs from the Middle East war were largely to blame for the higher CPI reading, with fast-rising software and toy prices also pointing to the impact of AI-driven demand and higher tariffs under Trump's trade policy. The rising cost of borrowing to buy a home is an added burden for many US households. The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose last week to 7.5%, the highest in nearly three years, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. The data for the latest Beige Book was collected on or before October 5.

item.title: Lamar Jackson idle, Ravens hopeful he's ready for Browns
item.description: Lamar Jackson was not made available to media for his typical Wednesday afternoon interview session, but signs point to the Ravens having their starting quarterback on the field Sunday against the Browns.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson was not made available to media for his typical Wednesday afternoon interview session, but signs point to the Ravens having their starting quarterback on the field Sunday against the Browns. Jackson was not on the field at the start of Wednesday's practice, but he has regularly been idle for the first workout of the week in past seasons. Jackson missed Week 5 recovering from an ankle injury that knocked him out of Baltimore's Week 4 win over the Titans in the first half. Tyler Huntley guided Baltimore to a win at Atlanta in Jackson's absence and will continue to take some reps with the starters this week. If he's able to suit up, Jackson will be going head-to-head with former Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken. The current Browns head coach said Wednesday he is preparing "for the Ravens" more than he's planning to stop Jackson. Monken did note the Ravens are slightly harder to defend at the moment with Jackson taking more snaps under center. Without a preset launch point in the pocket, defenses have to account for every angle with Jackson and be ready for bulldozing running back Derrick Henry to come straight downhill. Jackson did not practice last week but head coach Jesse Minter said the Ravens anticipated a shorter-term recovery period. Last week, Minter left the door open for Jackson to play even without practicing. --Field Level Media

item.title: GRANOS Soja retrocede en Chicago ante avance de la cosecha, a pesar del repunte de la demanda china
item.description: Los futuros del maíz y la soja estadounidenses bajaban el miércoles ya que el ritmo acelerado de la cosecha en el Medio Oeste aumentó la oferta, y se prevé que las condiciones meteorológicas sean en general favorables tras las lluvias caídas a mediados de semana en algunas zonas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los futuros del maíz y la soja estadounidenses bajaban el miércoles ya que el ritmo acelerado de la cosecha en el Medio Oeste aumentó la oferta, y se prevé que las condiciones meteorológicas sean en general favorables tras las lluvias caídas a mediados de semana en algunas zonas. La caída en la soja se vio limitada por la noticia de que China había adquirido varios cargamentos estadounidenses, en lo que supone la primera compra importante desde la reunión comercial de alto nivel celebrada el mes pasado. El trigo subía ligeramente debido a las preocupaciones sobre el suministro procedente de Rusia y Ucrania, ya que los ataques a buques de carga han interrumpido los envíos desde la región del Mar Negro. El maíz y la soja siguen apoyados por la intensa actividad de cosecha en todo el Medio Oeste. El Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos indicó que, al domingo, se había cosechado el 33% del maíz y el 46% de la soja del país, ya que los agricultores aprovecharon el tiempo más seco tras las lluvias que retrasaron la cosecha en septiembre. Las lluvias de esta semana han paralizado los trabajos en el campo, pero se espera que vuelva el clima más seco a finales de semana, según los meteorólogos. "Hoy hemos bajado debido al avance de la siembra y al hecho de que parece que vamos a tener buen clima de aquí en adelante. Pero nos mantenemos en niveles más bajos, dentro del rango de cotización. Los usuarios finales están intensificando sus compras en el mercado", afirmó Jack Scoville, analista de The Price Group. Los compradores del Gobierno chino contrataron entre 8 y 10 cargamentos de soja estadounidense el martes, dijeron operadores a Reuters. El Departamento de Agricultura estadounidense confirmó la mayor parte de las compras el miércoles en su comunicado diario de ventas de exportación. Los operadores están atentos a nuevas compras, ya que China se esfuerza por cumplir su compromiso de compra anual de 25 millones de toneladas métricas, en medio de la preocupación por el exceso de capacidad de trituración en el país. La Administración General de Aduanas de China informó de una caída del 7,7% en las importaciones de soja en septiembre. Los contratos de soja de noviembre de la Bolsa de Chicago bajaban 9 centavos a 12,7475 dólares por bushel a las 1715 GMT, mientras que los de maíz de diciembre cedían 3,50 centavos a 4,7925 dólares por bushel. El trigo de diciembre de la CBOT subía 2,50 centavos a 6,7175 dólares por bushel, tras conocerse la noticia de que dos buques de carga habían sido alcanzados por drones frente a la costa de Bulgaria.

item.title: Olivia Miles leads 6-player WNBA All-Rookie Team
item.description: Rookie of the Year and MVP runner-up Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx headline the six-player 2026 WNBA All-Rookie Team, announced Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rookie of the Year and MVP runner-up Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx headline the six-player 2026 WNBA All-Rookie Team, announced Wednesday. Miles was joined by No. 1 overall draft pick Azzi Fudd of the Dallas Wings, Seattle Storm guard Flau'Jae Johnson, Chicago Sky guard Sydney Taylor, Toronto Tempo guard Kiki Rice and New York Liberty guard Pauline Astier. Rice and Astier tied for fifth in the voting. Miles, the No. 2 overall pick, made the All-Star team and averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds in 40 games (all starts). Fudd averaged 13.1 points and shot 39.7% from 3-point range in 30 games (24 starts). Johnson averaged 14.9 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 42 games (all starts). Taylor, undrafted out of Louisville, posted 13.6 points and 2.0 assists in 37 games (26 starts). Rice averaged 13.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 28 games (20 starts) for the expansion Tempo. Astier, undrafted out of France, played all 44 games (39 starts) and tallied 9.3 points, 3.3 assists and 2.7 rebounds. --Field Level Media

item.title: BofA's mega-fine blunted by Team Trump history
item.description: A $1.2 bln penalty over compliance issues often rattles bank boards and shareholders. Just ask erstwhile CEOs of Citi, TD and Wells Fargo. Boss Brian Moynihan's money-laundering mess leaves him in comparatively tepid water, given the administration's vexing signals on wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Gandel
item.content:encoded: Aesop's "Boy Who Cried Wolf" will be a treasured tale for Bank of America (BAC.N) CEO Brian Moynihan. The mega-lender he runs just copped to violating the Bank Secrecy Act with a deficient anti-money-laundering program, transgressions that include a $1.2 billion fine. Compliance matters of this magnitude tend to unnerve boards and shareholders, but the Trump administration's past pronouncements on financial wrongdoing dilute the moral of this particular story. The US Treasury Department and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency unveiled enforcement action on Tuesday, accusing BofA of failing to report more than $5 billion of suspicious transactions in a timely manner. The agencies levied one of their biggest-ever penalties because, they said, Moynihan and his team put revenue ahead of addressing concerns raised by regulators before. BofA said it is [USN:O8N43T02A TEXT:""far along with and committed to completing""] the related issues and already absorbed many of the costs, including hundreds of millions of dollars during the third quarter. Moynihan has some damage control to do, but he may be in relatively tepid water compared to erstwhile counterparts. Citigroup's (C.N) Michael Corbat, Wells Fargo's John Stumpf (WFC.N) and TD Bank's Bharat Masrani (TD.TO) all left their respective CEO roles after running into similarly significant regulatory problems. President Donald Trump's vexing track record, however, probably gives Moynihan extra wiggle room. It's easy to question the motivations here. For one thing, Trump [USN:FWN3W42W4 TEXT:"pardoned"] Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who had pleaded guilty to anti-money-laundering violations and stepped down from the cryptocurrency exchange as part of a $4.3 billion settlement. Administration officials also have been echoing industry complaints that suspicious-activity reporting rules have become overly burdensome. Dubious probes like the one into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell have more than a whiff of political bullying. Moreover, just days into his second term, the president publicly [USN:S0N3OG012 TEXT:"rebuked"] Moynihan at the World Economic Forum in Davos for allegedly discriminating against conservative customers. Moynihan is under some justified pressure. BofA's share price gains have broadly under-performed the industry in recent years, prompting investors to push him to boost returns on tangible common equity into the high teens, even as some rivals already exceed 20%. The bank recently tried to [USN:L1N45V0WY TEXT:"reassure"] staff about deal-maker defections, Reuters reported this week. Even excluding the latest regulatory penalty, its third-quarter earnings would have declined, making it an outlier among large lenders. Although compliance shortcomings add to the CEO's challenges, the true extent of the problem is hard to discern because of who's shouting about them. As a result, Moynihan has scope to keep the real wolves at bay. Follow Stephen Gandel on LinkedIn and X . Bank of America on October 13 agreed to pay a $1.2 billion fine to settle accusations in a civil case brought by the financial crimes unit of the Treasury Department and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency that it failed to address previously flagged lapses in its anti-money-laundering controls. The US regulators said the bank failed to report in a timely way more than $5 billion of suspicious transactions to Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. As part of the settlement, BofA admits that it willfully violated the Bank Secrecy Act and failed to implement and maintain an anti-money-laundering program that met minimum regulatory requirements, Treasury said in a statement. BofA is required to work with a third party to identify and report suspicious transactions that were undetected and undergo an independent review of its suspicious activity monitoring and other programs, according to the consent order. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Vinicius Jr. ficará de fora de clássico contra Barcelona após suspensão de quatro partidas
item.description: Vinicius Jr. não poderá disputar o primeiro El Clásico, duelo que coloca frente à frente Real Madrid e Barcelona, da temporada, depois que a comissão disciplinar da Federação Espanhola de Futebol aplicou ao atacante brasileiro uma suspensão de quatro partidas nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vinicius Jr. não poderá disputar o primeiro El Clásico, duelo que coloca frente à frente Real Madrid e Barcelona, da temporada, depois que a comissão disciplinar da Federação Espanhola de Futebol aplicou ao atacante brasileiro uma suspensão de quatro partidas nesta quarta-feira. Vinicius foi expulso por puxar o cabelo de Nathan Saliba na vitória de 1 x 0 sobre o Villarreal, no sábado. A comissão impôs uma suspensão de duas partidas pela infração que resultou no cartão vermelho e acrescentou mais duas partidas por seus protestos contra o árbitro, de acordo com o relatório disciplinar referente à oitava rodada da LaLiga. A suspensão tira Vinícius das partidas do campeonato contra Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander e Valencia, deixando o técnico José Mourinho sem um de seus atacantes mais utilizados para a viagem ao Camp Nou. Vinicius foi titular em todas as partidas do Real nesta temporada, com exceção de uma. Ele pediu desculpas aos companheiros de equipe e aos torcedores do Real Madrid nas redes sociais após o incidente. O El Clásico acontece no dia 25 de outubro, quando o Real viaja para enfrentar o líder do campeonato, o Barcelona. As equipes estão separadas por seis pontos na tabela. (Reportagem de Ruairidh Barlow)

item.title: AI-powered stock funds bet bots can pick stocks faster and better than humans
item.description: A handful of fund managers are betting that exchange traded funds run by AI stock-picking models can crunch data quicker and make better investment decisions than humans, even as many people remain wary or even fearful of artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: A handful of fund managers are betting that exchange traded funds run by AI stock-picking models can crunch data quicker and make better investment decisions than humans, even as many people remain wary or even fearful of artificial intelligence. So far, fewer than half-a-dozen ETFs, collectively managing only about $30 million of the ETF industry's nearly $17 trillion in assets, rely solely on AI-powered bots to control everything from research to stock selection. While that represents a tiny fraction of the industry, AI is making its way slowly and steadily into the investment processes of most asset managers, to some extent, even if that may not yet be visible to investors themselves. Earlier this year, 91% of asset managers surveyed by Mercer reported plans to increase their use of AI-based portfolio management tools this year and said they are trying to figure out what tasks can be safely handed off to AI. The performance of the handful of funds that rely solely on AI to generate returns shows they are beating the market, even if their track records stretch back only a few months. Their managers argue these returns will attract more investments into the idea over time. "Until now you've had two choices: be a passive investor and own an index, or be an active investor" with a human picking stocks, said Tal Schwartz, founder and CEO of Ai Funds. "I want to offer a third option: where it's AI that is doing it all for you." In August, Schwartz launched the High Conviction US Equity AI-Managed ETF (HIAI.Z) , built on a proprietary AI learning algorithm that analyzes decades of market data. So far, it has attracted less than $20 million in assets, according to data from ETF.com, but Schwartz said it is still early days. AI can crunch more data more rapidly than any human being, he said, and strips human emotions and cognitive biases out of the investment process. "I know this is a long-term process, that people will only become convinced over time," he added. "I think that what will convince them is performance." Schwartz's fund is up 2.7% since its August 21 launch, beating the 1.1% gain for the S&P 500 index in the same time frame. Two funds [USN:L8N3Z61LG TEXT:"launched by Israeli asset manager"] FinQ in February have handily beaten the 11.0% gain by the S&P over that time frame. FinQ's dollar-neutral US Large-Cap AI-managed ETF (AINT.P) has soared 25.35% and the version of the ETF not offering a currency hedge is 23.98% higher since inception. Two other funds, the Pacer S&P 500 3AI Top 100 ETF (PSAI.Z) and the Pacer S&P World 3AI Top 100 ETF (WDAI.Z) , are ahead 10.34% and 10.33%, respectively, since their launches in early May, compared to a gain of 5.8% for the S&P 500. Nonetheless, advisers and analysts said the funds' short track records and above-average fees may limit investor interest. "Advisers are comfortable with AI that informs a decision and uneasy with AI that makes it," said Jeff Judge, a financial adviser at Chesapeake Financial Planners in Forest Hill, Maryland, adding his clients are not clamoring for this. "Proof that this approach works will really come down to who can thoughtfully manage risk and ride out a down market," said Todd Sohn, ETF analyst at Strategas. AI-ENHANCED ETFS MORE COMMON Other firms have rolled out "AI-enhanced" ETFs, which use AI to undertake quantitative analysis, analyze stocks or monitor risk. This cautious approach is more common, insiders said. "We've been training models using AI for seven or eight years now, and using them to run live capital for about four years," said David Wright, head of quantitative investments at Pictet Asset Management in Geneva. His firm launched the Pictet AI Enhanced US Equity ETF (PQUS.P) in February. Since its debut, the fund has attracted $163 million in assets and posted gains of 14.8%, compared to 11.4% for the S&P 500. Wright compares using AI in the investment process to using a plane's autopilot functions. The autopilot may be able to take off, cruise and land with no humans involved, but, he added, "I wouldn't go on a plane that didn't have a pilot." Other asset managers are taking a similarly cautious approach to integrating AI. "I'm not losing any sleep over robots ending the world," said Dan Taylor, deputy chief investment officer of systematic within Man Group, referring to recent headlines. "But I still do worry about AI's ability to deal with the most extreme, unlikely events, where all the action happens, both good and bad."

item.title: Valor global dos direitos de mídia esportiva atinge recorde de US$65,8 bilhões em 2026
item.description: O valor global dos direitos de mídia esportiva atingiu um recorde de US$65,82 bilhões em 2026, um aumento de 15% em relação a 2025, de acordo com o Relatório Global de Mídia Esportiva 2026 da SportBusiness, publicado nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Streisand Neto
item.content:encoded: O valor global dos direitos de mídia esportiva atingiu um recorde de US$65,82 bilhões em 2026, um aumento de 15% em relação a 2025, de acordo com o Relatório Global de Mídia Esportiva 2026 da SportBusiness, publicado nesta quarta-feira. Dois grandes eventos esportivos ocorreram em 2026: a Copa do Mundo de futebol na América do Norte e os Jogos Olímpicos de Inverno. O relatório prevê que o valor global dos direitos de transmissão esportiva cairá para US$62,2 bilhões em 2027. Em comparação com o valor de US$62,4 bilhões em 2024, ano dos Jogos Olímpicos de Paris, o crescimento em dois anos foi de 5%, segundo o relatório anual. Os EUA detêm grande parte do valor global dos direitos de mídia e agora representam 53,9% do total mundial, contra 46% em 2022. Os cinco maiores mercados da Europa, juntos, representam um terço do valor dos EUA. Os esportes norte-americanos, principalmente a Liga Nacional de Futebol (NFL) e a Associação Nacional de Basquete (NBA), respondem, juntos, por 30% do valor total global dos direitos de mídia. A Premier League inglesa responde por 7,8%, segundo o relatório.

item.title: Hope ton powers Windies to series-levelling win over India
item.description: Shai Hope struck another century as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth Twenty20 in Hyderabad on Wednesday to level the five-match series at 2-2.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shai Hope struck another century as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth Twenty20 in Hyderabad on Wednesday to level the five-match series at 2-2. Chasing 248, India made a brisk start with Sanju Samson racing to a half-century off 20 deliveries before falling to Keemo Paul for 56. Shreyas Iyer chipped in with 16 off 11 balls and Abhishek Sharma contributed 29 before Gudakesh Motie removed the opener. India accelerated again at the death through Nitish Kumar Reddy and Tilak Varma, who added 70 runs from 32 balls to keep the chase alive. Varma fell for 43 and Reddy was dismissed by Keemo Paul who triggered a collapse by claiming three wickets in the 19th over. India's tail folded quickly and the hosts were bowled out for 223. West Indies, put in to bat, made a brisk start with Jewel Andrew providing early impetus alongside captain Hope before Axar Patel trapped the opener LBW for 21 off 16 balls. Shimron Hetmyer and Hope added a rapid 58 runs, but Prince Yadav broke the stand with a caught-and-bowled effort to dismiss Hetmyer for a blistering 33 off 12 balls. Rovman Powell followed soon after, departing for 24. Hope remained unfazed, however, sharing an unbroken 91-run stand from 43 balls with Sherfane Rutherford who finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 deliveries. The hosts accelerated at the death, taking 22 runs off the 17th over to surge past the 200-run mark. Hope smashed an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls with four fours and nine sixes, reaching the milestone with a six off the final delivery as West Indies finished on 247 for three.

item.title: UN peacekeeping chief says talks on future of Lebanon mission must begin soon
item.description: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix on Wednesday urged the UN Security Council to begin negotiations on the future of peacekeepers deployed in Lebanon, as Beirut campaigns for an extension to the mandate set to expire at the end of this year.
item.dc:creator: Maya Gebeily
item.content:encoded: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix on Wednesday urged the UN Security Council to begin negotiations on the future of peacekeepers deployed in Lebanon, as Beirut campaigns for an extension to the mandate set to expire at the end of this year. A UN peacekeeping force known as UNIFIL has been deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978 but the Security Council last year ordered the mission to begin withdrawing at the end of 2026. Since a new war erupted in March between Israel and Iran-backed Lebanese armed group Hezbollah, the Lebanese government has campaigned for an extension to [USN:L6N45B03E TEXT:"UNIFIL's mandate"], citing its role in monitoring hostilities and facilitating [USN:L6N45502W TEXT:"aid deliveries"] to villages in Israeli-occupied zones. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres earlier this year [USN:L8N42A20H TEXT:"presented proposals"] for a continued uniformed UN presence in Lebanon but no action has been taken yet, Lacroix told Reuters in Beirut. "These proposals are on the table of the Security Council. There has been no movement in the Security Council until now, but I believe that the negotiations will begin ... shortly, in earnest," he said. "I think it would be better to have a decision soon rather than later, right? Because that would clarify also the horizon for us, certainly from the more limited point of view of our own planning," he said. FORCES OPERATE HOTLINE TO EASE TENSIONS Diplomats say the US is not supportive of an extended mandate for UNIFIL, but Lacroix said it was important to focus on Lebanon’s request and that negotiations at the Security Council could yield a constructive outcome. Some 7,500 UNIFIL peacekeepers are still deployed at about 50 positions in southern Lebanon, which would be expected to be handed over to Lebanese army troops if no new UN force is agreed. But since most of those posts lie in territory now occupied by the Israeli military, it remains unclear how Lebanese soldiers could deploy to take over the positions. Lacroix said that clarity on whether a new UN force would deploy to southern Lebanon would help UNIFIL make sure it does not "leave those positions prematurely before we know what could come next". In addition to facilitating aid deliveries and monitoring hostilities, the force operates a hotline to ease any tensions between the Lebanese and Israeli militaries. Lacroix said the deconfliction role was particularly crucial given the presence of Israeli troops in a self-declared security zone deep in Lebanese territory. He said that Israeli and Lebanese troops in the same geographic area presented "the risk of escalation, the risk of incidents getting out of control" and that "there is a need for a third party to de-escalate".

item.title: Brasil recebe US$2,415 bilhões líquidos na semana após o 1º turno, diz BC
item.description: O Brasil registrou fluxo cambial total positivo de US$3,214 bilhões em outubro até o dia 9, sendo que apenas na semana passada entraram no país US$2,415 bilhões líquidos, na esteira do resultado do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Brasil registrou fluxo cambial total positivo de US$3,214 bilhões em outubro até o dia 9, sendo que apenas na semana passada entraram no país US$2,415 bilhões líquidos, na esteira do resultado do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial. Após o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ficar à frente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no primeiro turno, houve na semana passada um forte avanço da bolsa brasileira e uma demanda maior por títulos brasileiros, em parte em função do fluxo de investimentos estrangeiros, o que também se refletiu na queda do dólar ante o real. Somente na semana passada -- entre 5 e 9 de outubro -- entraram no país US$4,127 bilhões pelo canal financeiro, que contabiliza investimentos estrangeiros diretos e em carteira, remessas de lucro e pagamento de juros, entre outras operações. Pelo canal comercial, que leva em conta exportações e importações, saíram do Brasil na semana passada US$1,711 bilhão. ACUMULADO DE OUTUBRO No acumulado de outubro até o dia 9, a entrada de recursos pelo canal financeiro somou US$4,087 bilhões, ante uma saída de US$872 milhões pela via comercial, mostraram os dados do BC. Os números são preliminares e fazem parte das estatísticas referentes ao câmbio contratado. Considerando o acumulado do ano até 9 de outubro, o Brasil registra fluxo cambial total positivo de US$13,916 bilhões.

item.title: Real Madrid's Vinicius to miss Clasico after four-game suspension
item.description: Vinicius Jr will miss Real Madrid's first Clasico of the season against Barcelona after the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee handed the Brazil forward a four-match suspension on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vinicius Jr will miss Real Madrid's first Clasico of the season against Barcelona after the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee handed the Brazil forward a four-match suspension on Wednesday. Vinicius was sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair after coming off the bench in Saturday's 1-0 win over Villarreal. The committee imposed a two-match ban for the red-card offence and added another two games for his protests to the referee, according to its disciplinary report for the eighth round of LaLiga fixtures. The suspension rules Vinicius out of league matches against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia, leaving coach Jose Mourinho without one of his most-used forwards for the trip to Camp Nou. Vinicius has started all but one of Real's matches this season. He [USN:L6N45W07P TEXT:"apologised"] to his teammates and Real Madrid fans on social media after the incident. The Clasico takes place on October 25, with Real travelling to face league leaders Barcelona. The teams are separated by six points in the table.

item.title: How does the US count measles deaths?
item.description: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has changed how the federal government recognizes deaths from measles in the midst of the worst US outbreak of the highly infectious virus in more than three decades, prompting backlash from disease experts and political opponents.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Lapid
item.content:encoded: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has changed how the federal government recognizes deaths from measles in the midst of the worst US outbreak of the highly infectious virus in more than three decades, prompting backlash from disease experts and political opponents. Here is what you need to know about how US measles deaths are currently determined: WHAT HAS CHANGED? For over a century, US state and local health officials have been required to report cases of death in people with a measles diagnosis to the federal government. These reports are separate from death certificates issued by hospital staff or coroners that can list measles as a cause of death or as a contributing factor. Disease experts have generally considered the death of any person infected with measles to be related to the virus, which can directly impair organs or exacerbate underlying health problems. Kennedy has said the US will no longer automatically include state reports to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention of people who died with measles in the national published tally of measles deaths. Instead, the CDC's National Center for Health Statistics will first confirm that measles was identified as an underlying cause of death on a person's death certificate — a process that can take weeks, according to health experts. The CDC has [USN:L4N45A17G TEXT:"also said"] it was re-evaluating how measles deaths are defined, without explaining the need for such a review. WHY IS KENNEDY'S CHANGE CONTROVERSIAL? After eradicating measles transmission within the country in 2000, the United States is now battling its biggest resurgence of the virus since 1991, fueled by rising vaccine hesitancy. More than 6,300 infections and at least eight fatalities have been reported by state and local officials since Kennedy, a longtime anti-vaccine activist, took the nation's top health job in early 2025. Kennedy, who spent years sowing doubt about the measles vaccine — by far the best way to prevent infection and spread of the disease — has cast doubt on whether measles can be fatal and promoted the theory that the virus is less dangerous than the vaccines used against it, contrary to decades of scientific evidence showing the benefits of the shots. He [USN:L6N45811F TEXT:"sparred publicly"] with Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, a Democrat, over the state's report of [USN:L4N45Y144 TEXT:"measles-related deaths"] before changing how such fatalities are counted. The CDC has so far accepted only two out of five measles-related deaths reported by US states so far this year. Leading medical organizations say Kennedy's comments and policies on immunization have increased Americans' distrust of vaccines, despite decades of evidence showing they are safe and effective at preventing disease. Disease experts say that the health secretary's questioning of measles death reports minimizes the risks of the virus, and that the change in how deaths are counted will delay information that could persuade more families to vaccinate their children. WHY ISN'T IT OBVIOUS WHEN SOMEONE DIED FROM MEASLES? Many infectious diseases kill indirectly. Measles, for example, can trigger complications such as croup, pneumonia and brain swelling that ultimately prove fatal. In some cases, deadly neurological complications don't appear until years after the infection. The virus can also induce immune system suppression that makes patients vulnerable to fatal secondary bacterial and viral infections. Death certificates generally record a chain of events. When a patient dies of respiratory failure due to pneumonia that was due to measles, the respiratory failure is the immediate cause of death, and measles is considered an underlying cause because it initiated the sequence of events leading to death. Local public health officials generally focus on the underlying cause because it reflects the disease responsible for setting the fatal process in motion. WHAT IF THE PERSON HAD OTHER SERIOUS HEALTH PROBLEMS? When a person with chronic lung disease, cancer, or another condition that makes them especially vulnerable to severe complications dies after a measles infection, the central question is usually whether the death would likely have occurred if the person had not contracted the virus. Investigators must determine whether measles caused the fatal deterioration, merely contributed to it, or was unrelated. Two experts reviewing the same medical records may sometimes emphasize different aspects of the case. That does not necessarily mean either side is acting improperly. Cause-of-death determinations often involve medical judgment. WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A MEASLES DEATH AND A MEASLES-ASSOCIATED DEATH? The term "measles-associated death" can reflect uncertainty about precisely how much the virus contributed. It allows health officials to acknowledge a connection when multiple factors were involved. ARE MEASLES DEATHS BEING OVERCOUNTED? There is no evidence that measles mortality is systematically overcounted. Historically, public health surveillance has focused on whether a disease caused or substantially contributed to death, rather than whether it was the sole factor involved. During the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, a similar debate took place over whether patients with preexisting chronic diseases were dying from COVID — that is, the SARS-CoV-2 virus caused the death — or with COVID, meaning they happened to have COVID but their cancer or other health condition is what killed them. Public health experts argue that excluding deaths simply because a patient had other medical problems would underestimate the disease's impact.

item.title: Lucrative tennis exhibition postponed amid Middle East conflict
item.description: The third edition of the Six Kings Slam, a high-stakes men's tennis exhibition in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, will not go off as scheduled next week amid tensions in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The third edition of the Six Kings Slam, a high-stakes men's tennis exhibition in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, will not go off as scheduled next week amid tensions in the Middle East. The six-player tournament was scheduled for Oct. 21, 22 and 24 and has been moved to Dec. 27-30, according to a statement shared Wednesday on X by Turki Al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority. The statement said the decision to reschedule the event came after "an assessment of the organizational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience." In Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, the King Khalid International Airport is closed after it was struck by drone and missile attacks attributed to Houthi rebels from Yemen during the past week. The New York Times reported that at least 14 people have been killed and hundreds more injured in the Iran-backed attacks. The tournament was set to include Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien, the latter a replacement for the injured Jannik Sinner. It is not known whether the players have committed to the replacement dates. Each participant is guaranteed an appearance fee of $1.5 million, with the winner earning an additional $4.5 million. Sinner walked away with $6 million in each of the event's first two years, defeating Alcaraz in the final both times. --Field Level Media

item.title: Atlantic Ocean currents can recover from severe climate weakening, study finds
item.description: An Atlantic Ocean current system weakened by global warming could recover over time if the climate cools, a study by the Danish Meteorological Institute showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Agnieszka Olenska, Louise Rasmussen
item.content:encoded: An Atlantic Ocean current system weakened by global warming could recover over time if the climate cools, a study by the Danish Meteorological Institute showed on Wednesday. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation brings warm water from the tropics northward toward the Arctic, and the flow of warm water helps keep Europe's winters mild. Published in the journal Science Advances, the study found no sign there was an irreversible tipping point for AMOC, as suggested by some previous studies, although the effects of the changes could last for centuries. However, it also said that the Greenland ice sheet that contributes to weakening the AMOC as it pours cold freshwater into the ocean could not be restored once it had melted — even if the warming trend was reversed. A disrupted AMOC could still destabilise global rainfall patterns and accelerate [USN:L6N3WM0K1 TEXT:"coastal sea-level rise"]. NO TIPPING POINT LEADING TO COLLAPSE SEEN IN MODEL The study said the AMOC could slow to about 6 million cubic metres of water per second from around 17 million at around 7 degrees Celsius of global warming. "In our model, we do not see a tipping point leading to a collapse. The AMOC gradually weakens, but we find that it also immediately regains its strength if global warming is reversed," lead author Chuncheng Guo said. However, he warned that even though recovery starts as soon as temperatures fall, it could take several centuries to finish, all while the effects of a weakened current would persist. The 7 C rise used in the modelling used for scientific interest is far beyond the current projections for the warming trend. The UN's environmental body said in September global temperature rises are set to exceed the key threshold of 1.5 C "within a few years". Governments committed to keeping temperature rises within 1.5 C to limit the impacts of extreme weather under the 2015 Paris Agreement. The cooling rate required to reverse the AMOC also exceeds what is considered realistic with current technology, Guo added, pointing to a limitation of the single-model study. Further testing against other models was also needed, the study said. Willem Huiskamp at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, who was not involved in the study, said a more stable AMOC would be good news, but said he doubted the real-world current was as stable as some models suggested. The researchers estimated a long-term sea-level rise of around 20 cm from the melting of the Greenland ice sheet following a 1.5 C rise, and urged faster action to rein in emissions. "Instead of relying on the global cooling to happen, it's a much, much safer strategy to not have warming in the first place," Guo said.

item.title: Juez federal bloquea la reorganización prevista de una agencia agrícola estadounidense
item.description: Un juez federal impidió el miércoles que el Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos siguiera adelante con la reorganización prevista de la agencia, lo que supone un revés para la amplia reforma del poder ejecutivo impulsada por el presidente Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: Un juez federal impidió el miércoles que el Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos siguiera adelante con la reorganización prevista de la agencia, lo que supone un revés para la amplia reforma del poder ejecutivo impulsada por el presidente Donald Trump. La sentencia del Tribunal de Distrito del Distrito Norte de California supone una victoria para los sindicatos que habían presentado una demanda para bloquear la iniciativa de reorganización, en parte porque los empleados afirmaban que debilitaría los servicios de la agencia. La orden detiene los esfuerzos de reorganización en varias agencias del USDA, entre ellas el Servicio de Investigación Agrícola, el Servicio Forestal, la Administración de Alimentación y Nutrición y otras. El juez Vince Chhabria señaló que la agencia estaba "reprogramando" los fondos del Congreso destinados a la reorganización, es decir, utilizando el dinero para un fin distinto al previsto. "El Congreso no contemplaba que el USDA utilizara los fondos que le habían sido asignados para cerrar oficinas o reubicar a empleados", escribió Chhabria. La iniciativa de reorganización de la agencia tenía como objetivo trasladar a unos 2.600 empleados de la región de Washington, así como consolidar las oficinas de la agencia en todo el país. El personal de la agencia había advertido que las salidas masivas de empleados a causa de la reorganización ponían en riesgo los programas de comercio, ayuda exterior, nutrición y otros. Un portavoz del USDA declaró: "El Departamento está analizando la decisión del juez y presentará su respuesta ante el tribunal". "El intento de la Administración de desmantelar esta agencia esencial es flagrantemente ilegal, y agradecemos que el tribunal haya impedido, por ahora, que se lleve a cabo un plan temerario", declaró Patrick Moran, presidente de la Federación Estadounidense de Empleados Estatales, del Condado y Municipales, en un comunicado.

item.title: Patriots open window for A.J. Brown; Christian Gonzalez ready to return
item.description: The New England Patriots have opened the 21-day practice window for wide receiver A.J. Brown, head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New England Patriots have opened the 21-day practice window for wide receiver A.J. Brown, head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. Brown has been sidelined since sustaining a high-ankle sprain during the second half of the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the teams' season opener on Sept. 9. He went on injured reserve two days later and missed the team's last four games. While Brown is working his way back to game action, Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez told reporters that he's ready to return to the field after missing two games due to a shoulder injury. "I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters Wednesday. Gonzalez, 24, signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension last month. He has started all 37 career games in which he has played -- including three this season -- since being selected by New England with the 17th overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Oregon. The Patriots host their AFC East rivals, the New York Jets, on Sunday. As for Brown, he sustained his injury after he was targeted by a third-down pass from Drake Maye, but Seahawks nickel cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett deflected the pass to force a punt. Pritchett's knee landed on the outside of Brown's ankle, which twisted inward as he went to the ground. Acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles via trade in early June, Brown had three receptions for a team-high 26 yards in the first half. Brown, 29, was named second-team All-Pro with the Eagles in 2022, 2023 and 2024. He has 527 receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns in 106 career games (98 starts) with the Tennessee Titans (2019-21), Eagles (2022-25) and Patriots. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) out multiple weeks
item.description: Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga will miss two to three weeks with an ankle injury, ESPN reported on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga will miss two to three weeks with an ankle injury, ESPN reported on Wednesday. The former All-Pro sustained the injury during Denver's 23-17 road win against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. Hufanga has been listed as a non-participant in practice this week and will likely be ruled out for Thursday night's game against the visiting Seattle Seahawks (3-2). Hufanga, 26, has recorded 23 tackles, two interceptions (one returned for a touchdown), a sack and a forced fumble through five starts for the Broncos (3-2). A fifth-round draft pick by San Francisco in 2021, Hufanga has 348 tackles, nine interceptions (two pick-sixes), five sacks and four forced fumbles in 71 career games (59 starts) with the 49ers (2021-24) and Broncos. He made the Pro Bowl and was named first-team All-Pro in 2022. The Denver depth chart at safety includes starter Brandon Jones, Devon Key, JL Skinner and Tycen Anderson. --Field Level Media

item.title: Los derechos de retransmisión deportiva alcanzaron un récord de 65.800 millones de dólares en 2026
item.description: El valor global de los derechos de retransmisión deportiva alcanzó un récord de 65.820 millones de dólares en 2026, un aumento del 15% frente al año previo, según el "SportBusiness Global Media Report 2026", gracias a dos grandes eventos: el Mundial de fútbol y los Juegos Olímpicos de Invierno.
item.dc:creator: Streisand Neto
item.content:encoded: El valor global de los derechos de retransmisión deportiva alcanzó un récord de 65.820 millones de dólares en 2026, un aumento del 15% frente al año previo, según el "SportBusiness Global Media Report 2026", gracias a dos grandes eventos: el Mundial de fútbol y los Juegos Olímpicos de Invierno. El informe, que se publicó el miércoles, prevé que el valor mundial de los derechos de retransmisión deportiva sumará 62.200 millones de dólares en 2027. En comparación con los 62.400 millones de dólares de 2024, el año de los Juegos Olímpicos de verano de París, el crecimiento en dos años ha sido del 5%, según el reporte anual. Estados Unidos concentra gran parte del valor mundial de los derechos de retransmisión y ahora representa el 53,9% del total mundial, frente al 46% de 2022. Los cinco mayores mercados europeos suman, en conjunto, un tercio del valor de Estados Unidos. Los deportes estadounidenses, sobre todo la NFL y la NBA, representan entre ambos el 30% del valor total de los derechos de retransmisión del mundo, mientras que la Premier League inglesa supone el 7,8%, según el informe.
